about: Definition of the multi-frame enabler-free Intel-free variant (how it works: packaging/public/ARCHITECTURE.md; the C side: src/game/mfg_proxy.c with XEFG_PROXY_MFG and src/game/mfg_proxy_coexist.h): the libxess_fg.dll proxy of release/intel_free_2x.json, but with the multi-frame support of the enabler-era Intel-free add-on (release/intel_free.json) kept, so Intel's runtime gets this project's replacement pipelines at whatever frame count it runs: 2x on its own, and 3x/4x when another module the user installed has lifted Intel's frame limit for GPUs other than its own. FreeFG lifts no limit and patches nothing in Intel's runtime. When another module has hooked Intel's entry points, the lifecycle entries tail-call Intel's (that module sees the caller it would see without this proxy), contexts this proxy does not accelerate get the caller's own device and queue, and a model census or order of work this project did not verify makes the context step aside (Intel's or that module's shaders) instead of ending the game. Read by release/build_proxy.py --variant intel-free-mfg and release/assemble.py --variant intel-free-mfg.
configuration: Enabler-free Intel-free add-on, multi-frame: libxess_fg.dll proxy over Intel's unmodified XeFG runtime (bc250_xefg_original.dll), own shaders only, at the frame count the runtime runs (multi-frame network, pooled model sets, retirement at frame-count changes, SDK-status pacing signal); beside another module hooking the runtime it keeps the callers of the lifecycle entries and steps aside instead of ending the game; no XeSSMFG enabler, MinHook or frame-start pacer

dropped_defines.XEFG_MFG_XELL_PACE=1: Frame-start pacer: it reads the factor from the enabler's ApplyMultiplier hook and inline-hooks XeLL and the SDK's Present. This build hooks nothing; a module that lifts Intel's frame limit paces frame starts itself, and two pacers on Intel's Present would conflict. The pacing layer still learns when XeFG generates (accelerated counters and the SDK's present status).
dropped_defines.XEFG_MFG_NO_ENABLER_UI=1: Hook on the enabler's overlay; no enabler.

kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_RESEARCH=1: Multi-frame network and its model census (the 2x, multi-frame or both model sets; mfg-finish kernels; late model sets).
kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_POOL=1: Pooled model sets and pipelines for the sets and pipelines Intel's runtime recreates at a frame-count change.
kept_defines.XEFG_MFG_RETIRE=1: Heap and list retirement after a frame-count change (xefgSwapChainSetNumInterpolatedFrames), instead of the enabler's ApplyMultiplier.
kept_defines.XEFG_FRAME_CAP_RESEARCH=1: Inert in the Intel-free build (scaling forced off); compiled in because retirement reads its frame tracking, as in the enabler-era Intel-free add-on.
kept_defines.XEFG_FLOW_CAP_RESEARCH=1: Inert in the Intel-free build; compiled in for the same reason.

added_defines.XEFG_F4Q=1: F4Q (FreeFG 1.1): this project's FP32 Winograd F(4x4,3x3) kernels for the U-Net decoder b3941ac8 and encoder f030948d in place of its F(2x2) kernels, on by default (src/model_f4q.h, src/game/f4q.h; profile "add"). Their outputs matched the F(2x2) kernels' in every test, which does not prove every input. BC250_XEFG_F4Q=0, or F4Q=0 in BC250-XeFG/settings.ini, turns them off; BC250_XEFG_F4Q_SHADOW=1 is a diagnostic that runs them beside the F(2x2) kernels and counts equal and differing outputs on the GPU.

profile.name: cl-wino-q33-intel-free-mfg
profile.replace_about: Files of the Intel-free profile this build ships in another form of this project's own, from the inputs.lock.json tree group "own_files" (release/profile-mfg; recipes in its origin.json, rebuilt by release/build_profile.py check): the file takes the new bytes, and its waves.txt line (the same wave size) names the new module in place of the old one, so the table keeps its length and order (release/build_proxy.py prepare_profile). XU-1 (FreeFG 1.1): the nine U-Net shaders of wino_rs16.hlsl, wino_enc16.hlsl and wino_dec16.hlsl compiled with XU1=1 and -enable-16bit-types (the input transform in FP16 pairs, exact for the transform's small integers; in wino_rs16 also a wave-uniform epilogue). The FP32 products and sums are the release recipe's, so the outputs are the same: each kernel checked on the CPU (DXIL, lavapipe), and the generated images identical on all 20 SDK test rows on the BC-250 (2026-10-20). The two wino_row16 shaders keep their release recipe (XU1 measured slower there). release/profile itself, which the 2x build (0.9.0) and the enabler-era Intel-free add-on read, is not changed.
profile.add_about: Files of this project's own this build ships beside the Intel-free profile, from the same tree group (release/profile-mfg), with a waves.txt line appended after the append_waves lines when they have a wave size. F4Q (FreeFG 1.1, XEFG_F4Q): the FP32 Winograd F(4x4,3x3) kernels the proxy loads in place of the F(2x2) <hash>.dxil of b3941ac8 and f030948d while F4Q is on (src/game/f4q.h), and the check kernels of its diagnostic (BC250_XEFG_F4Q_SHADOW=1). The F(4x4) kernels are byte-identical to the ones round 3 tested: 20 of 20 SDK test rows identical, 96,480 in-game comparisons with 0 differing (Cyberpunk 2077, native 2x and OptiScaler 3x), 0.19-0.28 ms less GPU time per generated frame than the F(2x2) kernels on those two pipelines. Identical in every test, not proven for every input.

f4q-check-uav-float.dxil.about: F4Q check: fingerprint of a UNORM/FLOAT view (KIND 1)

f4q-check-uav-sint.dxil.about: F4Q check: fingerprint of a SINT view (KIND 2)

f4q-check-uav-raw.dxil.about: F4Q check: fingerprint of a buffer view's words (KIND 3)

f4q-check-aux.dxil.about: F4Q check: clear, compare and stamp passes (KIND 4)

profile.append_waves_about: Lines appended to the profile's waves.txt (release/build_proxy.py prepare_profile; release/profile/waves.txt itself stays the pinned table, whose bytes remain the prefix): wave 32 for five of Intel's unchanged pipelines that run in this build where the full profile had Intel-derived replacements (release/INTEL-FREE.md), so their wave size was never chosen. The pacing layer requests it from the driver by module hash on the BC-250 only; the shader code is not changed. Measured 2026-10-20 on the BC-250: generated images identical on all 20 SDK test rows (SDR and HDR10, engine and pixel motion vectors, 1440p and 4K), 0.07-0.08 ms less GPU time per generated frame in SDR and 0.18 ms in HDR10. The pacing layer then reads 128 entries; one malformed or repeated line would make it drop the whole table, which prepare_profile refuses. The 2x variant (0.9.0) and the enabler-era Intel-free add-on keep the pinned table, so their reference builds stay reproducible.
